$comment: Hand-maintained inputs for scripts/standards/build.mjs. Outcome and indicator text is NOT here; it is parsed from data/sources. Evidence items are Readyline guidance (draft until the PO reviews them), not Commission text.
evidenceDisclaimer: Evidence items are Readyline guidance on what auditors typically ask to see. They are not part of the NDIS Practice Standards and do not replace the auditor's own scope of audit.

evidenceReview.note: All evidence items reviewed and approved by the product owner (REQ-005 PO review, 12 Oct 2026). Items added later carry draft: true until reviewed.

changelog.note: First full dataset: core module, the six legacy supplementary modules, the SIL module effective 1 July 2026, the verification module, all 38 registration classes with audit type and modules, and derivation rules. Sources fetched 2026-10-11.

Evidence items reviewed by the product owner: all approved, draft flags cleared, reviewedBy and reviewedAt recorded. Three additions: signed Code of Conduct acknowledgement record under core and verification human resource management; worker screening clearance register under verification human resource management. No change to Commission text or sources.

NDIS watch 13 October 2026 (batch 35, items 7 and 8): the SIL quality indicators are also in the amending instrument F2026N00443 (Part 8A, Module 5A, ss 72A to 72E, commenced 1 July 2026), added as a source for the SIL module and class 0138; the 0138 note puts the 1 October 2026 application deadline in the past tense. No change to Commission text, standards or evidence items.

modules.name: Core module
modules.appliesTo: a core module that applies to all registered NDIS providers delivering higher-risk supports and services

modules.name: High intensity daily personal activities module
modules.appliesTo: When a provider is supporting participants who rely on high intensity daily personal activities, they need to make sure their workers have the skills and knowledge described in the high intensity support skills descriptors. To be registered for the class of support (registration group) 104 - high intensity daily personal activities, a provider must be assessed against the relevant NDIS Practice Standards contained in Module 1 of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.

modules.name: Specialist behaviour support module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are registered to provide specialist behaviour support to NDIS participants.

modules.name: Implementing behaviour support plans module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are registered to provide specialist behaviour support to NDIS participants. They also apply to providers using restrictive practices in the delivery of any NDIS supports and services.

modules.name: Early childhood supports module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are registered to provide early childhood supports to NDIS participants.

modules.name: Specialised support coordination module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are registered to provide specialist support co-ordination to NDIS participants.

modules.name: Specialist disability accommodation module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are registered to provide specialist disability accommodation to NDIS participants.

modules.name: Supported independent living (SIL) module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are registered to provide Supported Independent Living to NDIS participants.

modules.name: Verification module
modules.appliesTo: These NDIS Practice Standards apply to NDIS providers who are delivering lower risk/lower complexity supports and services.

registrationGroups.name: Assistance to access and maintain employment or higher education
Assistive products for personal care and safety
High Intensity Daily Personal Activities
registrationGroups.notes: Workers are assessed against the high intensity support skills descriptors. Only the high intensity activities listed on the certificate of registration may be provided.

registrationGroups.name: Assistance in coordinating or managing life stages, transitions and supports
Specialist positive behaviour support
registrationGroups.notes: Registration is required to provide specialist behaviour support services.

registrationGroups.name: Assistance with daily life tasks in a group or shared living arrangement
registrationGroups.notes: Providers registered for 0115 who deliver supported independent living have a dedicated transition pathway to class 0138 on the Commission's SIL transition page.

registrationGroups.name: Development of daily living and life skills
registrationGroups.notes: The Registration Requirements PDF lists this class as 'Development of daily care and life skills'; the audit-type table's name is used here.

registrationGroups.name: Early intervention supports for early childhood
registrationGroups.notes: An individual or partnership whose only certification class is early childhood is assessed under modified certification: the core module's freedom from violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination outcome only, plus the early childhood module (rules.modifiedCertification).

registrationGroups.name: Participation in community, social and civic activities
Management of funding for supports in participant plans
registrationGroups.notes: Plan management providers must give the auditor a list of workers delivering plan management, certified copies of their qualifications and professional memberships per the Qualification and Professional Associations Required Documentation Guide, and worker screening clearances for each worker. Registration is required to provide plan management services.

registrationGroups.name: Specialist disability accommodation
registrationGroups.notes: SDA alone is assessed against the SDA module without the core module; SDA with any other class adds the core module (rules.coreExemptWhenSole). Registration is required to provide SDA.

registrationGroups.name: Group and centre-based activities
registrationGroups.notes: Spelled 'Group and centre-based activities' in the Registration Requirements PDF; the audit-type table's spelling is used here.

registrationGroups.name: Providing an NDIS digital platform service
registrationGroups.notes: Mandatory registration from 1 July 2026. Registered NDIS digital platform providers need a certification audit, the core module and specific conditions of registration for NDIS digital platforms (section 13D of the Provider Registration Rules). The platform definition is summarised in the Commission's transition page; the Rules hold the full definition.

registrationGroups.name: Assistance with supported independent living
registrationGroups.notes: Mandatory registration from 1 July 2026. Registered SIL providers need a certification audit, the core module and the SIL supplementary module. Providers already delivering SIL had to apply for registration by 1 October 2026 or stop providing SIL supports; a new SIL entrant cannot provide SIL while an application is pending (Commission explanatory document, June 2026, read 13 October 2026). Whether supports are SIL depends on the Commission's definition and exclusions (rules.silDefinition).

exemptions: an individual or partnership that only required a certification audit to provide early intervention supports for early childhood
a provider that is only registered to provide specialist disability accommodation

ratings.label: conforms with elements of best practice

appliesWhen: the person with disability requires support at all times of the day, or for most of the day

the assistance provided helps the person with disability to live in their home as autonomously as possible and access the community, by: assisting with daily life tasks, or supervising daily life tasks
the provider is managing and delivering supported independent living supports. Providers make sure the participant receives home and living support in accordance with the package of supports.
notSilWhen: a person only receives a few hours of support a day or week, or
a person chooses and manages their own support workers (this includes directing, planning and rostering their own support workers).

businessDay.$comment: REQ-032 D-2914 (Dev-1, 2026-10-18): the meaning of business day in the Rules, verified against the instruments on legislation.gov.au.
businessDay.definition: business day means a day that is not a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the place concerned.
businessDay.instrument: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 2B, Compilation No. 39 (28 March 2026)

s 5 defines twenty-six terms, not business day; business days used in s 17(2)(b)
